notes:
Summary: Meridian is a mid-market contact center vendor that sells cloud and on-prem orchestration software to telco and retail customers. They evaluate Redwood for agent assist + reliability under spikes. Main ask: guarantee degraded-but-live behavior under 3x baseline surge and ability to run POC in VPC/on-prem staging.

Key quotes / customer color:
- 'If we drop callers during Black Friday we lose enterprise deals — need graceful degradation.'
- 'Tool-calling (CRM writes, ticket creation) must not be lost during queue backpressure; retries and idempotency required.'

POC scope (what we're validating):
- Throughput: sustain 3k concurrent active agent sessions with mixed chat/voice transcript generation at 300 rps baseline, 900 rps surge window (3x).
- Latency targets: 95th token latency < 120ms in dedicated mode; acceptable degraded mode < 300ms.
- Failure modes: simulate region outage, capacity saturation; verify automatic fallback to smaller quantized model and cross-region routing.
- Tooling: agent-assist suggestions, auto-summarization for ticket creation, automated CRM tool-calls for escalate/create_ticket. Validate exactly-once semantics for ticket writes.

Security/compliance notes:
- Legal requires audit logs for model outputs tied to request id (retention 7 years for some telco customers).
- Prefer customer-managed KMS and VPC peering; on-prem packaging needed for two strategic customers in EU.

Commercial / pricing notes:
- Meridian expects blended pricing: reserved capacity for peak windows + burst credits. Looking for a predictable per-concurrent-session metric.

Internal open items for Redwood rep:
- Provide deterministic benchmark docs for 3x spike (link to perf playbook).
- Confirm KMS/HSM integration timeline for Q3.
- Draft canary rollout plan for model fallback and operator runbooks.

Stubs / links referenced in conversation: Fireflies ff-2026-01-14-1352 (intro call), ff-2026-02-19-0930 (technical deep dive). Drive deck link above. Jira INF-3421 is note about load-generator config; SEC-9982 is legal question about recording retention.
